title: Demonstrationes circa residua ex divisione potestatum per numeros primos resultantia

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the 'Conclusiones' that open E449, Euler's deductive reworking of the theory of power residues of a geometric progression 1, a, a^2, ... modulo a prime P. The aim of the paper is Fermat's little theorem and the structure of the cycle of residues.

§3: If gcd(a,P)=1, then no power a^k is divisible by the prime P, so 0 never occurs among the residues. This is Euclid's lemma applied to a^k.

§4: Every residue lies in {1,...,P-1}, a set of P-1 elements. So at most P-1 distinct residues can occur, and since the sequence is infinite, residues must recur (pigeonhole principle).

§5: Successive residues satisfy a recursion. If ε = a^5 - mP and ζ = a^6 - nP, then ζ - aε = (ma-n)P, so ζ = aε - (n-ma)P. In modern terms, r_{k+1} ≡ a·r_k (mod P): the next residue is a·r_k reduced mod P. Combined with §4, this implies (though Euler does not yet say so here) that the sequence is eventually periodic, and in fact purely periodic once a recurrence is found.

§6-7: The integers are partitioned into P 'ordines' according to their remainder on division by P, listed as I: mP; II: mP+1; III: mP+2; IV: mP+3; and so on. These are the residue classes Z/PZ. Each class is determined by its least nonnegative member, the residue, which stands first in its row.

The next page (§8-9) adds that any member of a class may represent it, including negative ones, so residues can be taken in the symmetric range |r| ≤ P/2. That is the preparation for working mod P with representatives.

Overall the page sets up the elementary framework (residue classes, multiplicative recursion, finiteness) needed for the later proofs on period length and a^(P-1) ≡ 1.
errors: No mathematical errors. §5 algebra checked: (a^6 - nP) - a(a^5 - mP) = (ma-n)P, correct.

Minor gap: §4 only shows that some residue repeats. Pure periodicity from the start needs the recursion of §5 plus invertibility of a mod P (or cancellation). Euler supplies this later in the paper, not on this page.

ideas.what: Powers of a number prime to a prime P are never divisible by P; zero never occurs as a residue
ideas.modern_name: Euclid's lemma / a is a unit in Z/PZ
ideas.where_published: E262 (Theoremata circa residua ex divisione potestatum relicta, 1761) and E271 (Theoremata arithmetica nova methodo demonstrata)

ideas.what: Finitely many possible residues force repetition in the infinite sequence of residues
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Euler and Lagrange used it in this context

ideas.what: Next residue obtained by multiplying the current residue by a and reducing mod P
ideas.modern_name: r_{k+1} ≡ a r_k (mod P); modular exponentiation by repeated multiplication

ideas.what: Partition of the integers into P classes by remainder, each represented by its least member
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801), for the congruence notation; Euler for the class ('ordo') concept
ideas.where_published: E271 and Euler's tract De numerorum doctrina (E792, posthumous); also discussed by Weil, Number Theory: An Approach through History

deep.surprise_reason: Purely foundational material (residue classes, recursion, pigeonhole), already present in Euler's earlier residue papers and well documented in the historical literature.
transcription_corrections: Row I in the image reads '0, P  2P, 3P, ...' with a missing comma after P (printing quirk); the transcription normalizes this.
Row IV ends 'mP,+3' in print (stray comma); the intended text is mP+3.
§7 'ordine' is printed slightly damaged ('ord'ne'); the transcription is correct.
